description: App development for Islamabad companies and founders: iOS, Android and web apps with JazzCash, Easypaisa and card payments, built for real networks.
h1: App development for Islamabad companies, communities and founders
intro: 22 Signals handles app development for Islamabad companies and founders: iOS and Android apps, web apps and SaaS products, from MVP to app store launch. We build for mid-range phones and patchy connections, connect JazzCash, Easypaisa, Raast and card payments through licensed providers, and stay on after launch to support and improve the product.

sections.h: Apps that have to work on a mid-range phone and a busy network
p: An app that runs beautifully on a developer's new iPhone in an air-conditioned office can fall apart on a three-year-old Android on mobile data in a crowded market. In Pakistan most of your users carry Android phones, often with limited storage, and connections drop at the worst moment. Good app development for Islamabad users starts from that reality.

We keep apps small, cache what users need, retry gracefully when the network drops and test on the kind of phones your customers actually own. Then we make sure the same product works for your iPhone users and your web users too.

Field teams need even more. Development programmes and research projects run out of Islamabad often send staff to districts where coverage is weak or absent. Their apps have to keep working without a connection: forms saved on the device, photos and GPS points stored safely, and everything synced when the phone finds a signal again, with conflicts handled rather than overwritten. Personal data on the device is encrypted, and lost phones can be locked out remotely.

p: Pakistani users expect to pay the way they already do: mobile wallets such as JazzCash and Easypaisa, bank transfers through Raast, the State Bank of Pakistan's instant payment system, and debit or credit cards. We integrate through licensed payment providers and their official APIs, so your app never holds customer funds itself.

If your product moves money in a more central way, such as a wallet, lending or a marketplace that pays out, State Bank of Pakistan rules for fintech and electronic money apply. We help you understand which questions to take to a lawyer and to the provider before a line of payment code is written.

sections.h: Before app development: Islamabad founders' first questions
p: We ask every client to settle a few things before any app development. Islamabad founders who skip this step usually pay for it later in rework:
list: Who are the first hundred users, and how will you reach them?
Does the interface need Urdu, English or both, and will Urdu screens read right to left?
Will people sign in with a phone number, and should one-time codes go by SMS or WhatsApp?
What personal data does the app collect, and where will it be stored?
Which single number tells you the first release worked?
Talk: what problem the app solves, for whom, and how you will know it is working
Plan: features ranked into a first release and later ones, screen designs and a written timeline
Build: development in short cycles with test builds on your phone every couple of weeks
Grow: launch, crash and usage monitoring, updates and new features, with one Signal Lead throughout

p: We built a client portal with document sharing and payments for a US law firm, which handles sensitive files and money for clients who are not technical. The same habits carry into every app we build: plain screens, clear status messages, secure storage and payments that reconcile.

We work with founders and companies in Islamabad remotely from our head office in London. Test builds arrive through TestFlight and Google Play internal testing, so your team tries every version on real phones. Sprint reviews sit in the Islamabad afternoon; 12:00 London is 17:00 PKT in winter and 16:00 PKT in summer, which still leaves time for questions before the day ends.
Quick questions go to WhatsApp, decisions go in writing. When user testing with real customers in Islamabad or Rawalpindi would help, we plan it with you and visit when the project needs it.

faqs.q: Should we build native or cross-platform?
faqs.a: For most business apps, cross-platform frameworks such as Flutter or React Native give you iOS and Android from one codebase and keep cost and timelines down. Native development makes sense for heavy graphics, deep hardware access or very demanding performance. We recommend one after hearing what the app must do and how long it needs to last.

faqs.q: Can you integrate JazzCash and Easypaisa?
faqs.a: Yes, through their official merchant APIs or through a payment aggregator that bundles wallets, Raast and cards. You will need a merchant account in your organisation's name, which we help you apply for. We test every payment path, including failed and refunded payments, before launch.

faqs.q: How long does an MVP take?
faqs.a: It depends on what the first version must do. We agree a short, focused feature list that tests your main idea, set the launch date in writing during the Plan stage, and send test builds throughout so you see progress. Scope added later moves the date, and we tell you that before agreeing to it.

faqs.q: Who owns the code and the app store accounts?
faqs.a: You do. Apps are published under your own Google Play and Apple developer accounts, the code lives in a repository your organisation owns, and we hand over documentation. That way you can bring development in-house or change supplier later without starting again.

faqs.q: Do you work with National Incubation Center startups?
faqs.a: Yes, though most of our clients are established companies. For founders in Islamabad, we usually scope a lean MVP that answers one question with real users, then plan the next stage from what they do. We are honest when an idea needs validating with a landing page or a prototype before anyone writes app code.

faqs.q: Can we meet you in Islamabad?
faqs.a: We work with Islamabad clients over video calls and shared test builds, from our head office in London. We do not have an Islamabad office. For workshops or user testing that need people in the room, we plan a visit when the project needs it and agree it in advance.
